reported_as_is_context.text: ASCEND is associated with student rocketry and avionics teams. The club uses tasks approved by senior members and PDR, CDR and FRR gates.
reported_as_is_context.interpretation_limit: Club practice is not evidence that all ASCEND EPS activities follow these gates.

exact_source_lines.text: ASCEND is currently associated to a Rocketry Team and an Avionics Team of a student club.
The Rocketry Team operates on requirements given by Rocketry Competition Organizers.
The requirements are stated in terms of the target maximum height or maximum acceleration of the rocket.
One competition imposed the requirement of launching and returning to ground an egg without breaking it, which can only be validated via demonstration.
The Team Captains convert the requirements of a competition to atomic tasks.
Tasks are performed by any club member and approved by senior members.
The club performs the PDR, CDR, and FRR review gates.

reported_as_is_context.text: Observed club development emphasizes reuse and atomic edits. Battery sizing used component datasheet on/off power and estimated duty cycles.
reported_as_is_context.interpretation_limit: This is a rocket payload example, not proof of CubeSat mission analysis at ASCEND.

exact_source_lines.text: There is a large emphasis on technology reuse at the club, so most tasks are formulated as atomic edits to existing designs.
Furthermore, most of the tasks for a particular competition involve development activities like PCB manufacturing, soldering, and assembly.

One observed task involved adding a COTS to a PCB, which was specified in the task title. The task was broken down into subtasks, one of which required to connect a capacitor to the COTS, possibly prescribed by its datasheet.
The competition requirements include the radio communications technologies allowed for rocket launch commands and telemetry.
Thus, radio transceivers are some of the first COTS chosen for rocket designs.

The egg mission also introduced a payload consisting of 1U unit with a mechanically damping material to protect the egg, and heat pumps to maintain its temperature within a range inspired by an incubator machine.
Multiple lithium-ion cells were used to power the latest revision of the egg incubator payload.

To size them, a power budget was generated by consulting the datasheets of the already chosen components and extracting "on" and "off" power consumption values, then estimating the duty cycle of each component for one launch.
The duty cycle of telemetry components is estimated from the telemetry frequency requirements of the competition. For the rest of the components, it is conservatively assumed that they are always on.

reported_as_is_context.text: Observed payload power interfaces and battery endurance checks used assembled hardware, realistic telemetry and a controlled temperature environment.
reported_as_is_context.interpretation_limit: Representative conditions and the reported several-fold endurance margin do not validate a new EPS model.

exact_source_lines.text: A PCB design was observed consisting of multiple boards connected perpendicularly via PCI to a backplane that was the size of a 1U face.
Status indicator LEDs were observed for 3.3 and 5 volt buses.
The power source of the payload is verified experimentally.
The payload is fully assembled and set to provide telemetry at a realistic frequency while powered by the battery.

It is then inserted into a temperature controlled environment like a refrigerator so the heat pumps can be observed under representative operation conditions, and left to operate until the battery power runs out.
If the time from experiment start to power depletion is greater than the mission period, the power requirements are taken to be verified.
In practice, the battery life is several times larger than the mission period.

reported_as_is_context.text: The egg payload uses measured accelerations and drops for damping iteration. OpenRocket analyses support rocket height and acceleration checks before development.
reported_as_is_context.interpretation_limit: Transferable workflow precedent, not EPS verification evidence.

exact_source_lines.text: The demonstratable requirement to protect an egg has been related to the measurable variable of acceleration in the egg chamber. An IMU was placed inside this chamber, which is mechanically damped, and another in a rigid point of the payload chassis.
The difference in acceleration between the two IMUs during realistic launches is analyzed to iterative on the damping design.
Launches are recreated by manually dropping the payload from a representative height.
The drop data, and naturally an inspection of the egg, is used to characterize the damping as "too soft" or "too hard".
Maximum rocket height and maximum rocket acceleration requirements are verified at the design phase using the OpenRocket software.
This software works with abstract representations of rocket components (nose, stages, etc.) can be parametrized, combined, and then simulated.
Rocket height and acceleration requirements are taken to be verified based on the results of the simulatins, and only then does development start.

reported_as_is_context.text: The club reports about two months of onboarding. ASCEND researchers report nine months on one EPS requirements-to-high-level-design iteration.
reported_as_is_context.interpretation_limit: No sample distribution, task-normalized comparison, or causal attribution supports new framework performance thresholds.

exact_source_lines.text: The club reports that it takes about 2 months to onboard new members to the point where they can complete tasks.

Separately, ASCEND researchers have spent 9 months on one iteration of an EPS design following a more traditional systems engineering approach, starting from requirements and currently advenced up to high-level design, with a power budget completed and battery and panel options compared but no component selections yet.

intro_context.claim: Early EPS evidence fragmentation hinders traceability, reproducibility and issue detection.

exact_source_lines.text: Evidence fragmentation during the early lifecycle phases of nanosatellite electrical power systems hinders the traceability between needs and requirements, architecture decisions, and the analytical evidence that supports them. Furthermore, it hinfers the reproducibility of analyses and the capability to detect design inconsistencies before advacing to physical verification and validation phases.

intro_context.claim: Characterize EPS needs, requirements, interfaces and criteria. Define framework flow. Provide generic EPS functions, logical/physical elements, modes/states and requirements. Characterize early EPS V&V. Evaluate two contrasting cases.

exact_source_lines.text: An MBSE framework is defined following Buruso et al. \cite{buruso2026modelbased} as the integration of MBSE methods, MBSE languages, and MBSE tools within and throughout the relevant lifecycle phases. The secondary objectives of this project are: to characterize the needs, requirements, interfaces and technical criteria of nanosatellite EPS; to define the operational flow of modeling, analysis, and evidence management of the MBSE framework; to model a generic EPS architecture with functions, logical and physical components, interfaces, modes and states, and requirements; to characterize early EPS verification and validation within the EPS framework; to evaluate the framework on two contrasting EPS case studies.

intro_context.claim: Verify evidence chains, reproduction, discrepancy handling and two-case reuse. Measure correct change time, adaptation/reproduction/adoption effort, direct cost and detection accuracy against a qualified person.

exact_source_lines.text: It will be verified that the framework satifies the requirements imposed on it, including, among other, to maintaince valid evidence chains, to reproduce EPS analyses, identify and manage critical discrepancies, and to complete the two case studies without introducing post hoc modifications to the framework.

The fulfillment of requirements is associated to quantitative metrics, which include the time taken to correctly process a change, the effort (person-hours) required to adapt the framework to a case study, the effort needed to reproduce an analysis independently, adoption effort, direct usage cost, and the accuracy to detect inconsistencies (compared to a qualified person).

The two case studies will allow to determine whether the same framework core can be applied to contrasting EPS configurations, preserving the traceability and reproducibility of the generated evidence.

boundary_items.EX-01: Candidate count, design-change frequency, and failed external verification gates are inputs and external drivers. The framework manages impact and evidence. It cannot guarantee fewer changes or gates.
boundary_items.EX-02: Redesign cost, actual thermal/EMC/power defects, and hardware fabrication are external outcomes. The framework supports early analysis and exposes absent evidence. Physical qualification remains separate.
boundary_items.EX-03: Mission troubleshooting and the cost of physical EPS replicas occur after this project early-phase scope. Retained model and measurement evidence supports future troubleshooting. Replacement of replicas is unverified.
boundary_items.EX-04: Actual CubeSat RAM depends on hardware, software, mission conditions and operations. Framework acceptance covers RAM requirements, transformations and evidence, not achieved spacecraft reliability.
boundary_items.EX-05: The proportion verified by testing is governed by applicable requirements and model credibility. Analysis is used when justified. The framework does not force substitution of analysis for mandatory physical tests.
boundary_items.EX-06: Complete non-EPS subsystem acceptance is external. The framework covers EPS-facing demand, supply/protection interactions, interface data and associated evidence.

mission_needs.title: Write and maintain verifiable requirements
mission_needs.text: Enable engineers to learn requirement writing and maintain sourced, verifiable requirements with reusable templates and verification criteria.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The EPS engineering enterprise shall produce reviewable framework-supported EPS and component requirements whose source, observable quantities or conditions, verification method, criterion, and unresolved decisions are explicit.
mission_needs.moe: Requirement authoring and update effort (person-hours). Report defects found by a qualified reviewer and completeness against the declared requirement record schema.

mission_needs.title: Maintain a consistent evidence chain through changes
mission_needs.text: Keep needs, requirements, design decisions, subsystem allocations, models, software interfaces, and verification evidence consistent as EPS and other subsystem designs change.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall identify the affected evidence for each designated change and issue a successor baseline with regenerated or explicitly stale evidence and retained discrepancy status.
mission_needs.moe: Correct change turnaround (elapsed hours) and active effort. On a blinded reference set report TP, FP, FN and affected-artifact accuracy against a qualified reviewer. Faster incomplete changes receive no comparative credit.

mission_needs.title: Maintain candidate BOMs and financial estimates
mission_needs.text: Maintain bills of materials and cost estimates across EPS candidate architectures and controlled design changes.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall obtain a revision-linked BOM and financial estimate for each designated EPS candidate, with sourced prices, quantities, assumptions, uncertainty, and missing cost data visible.
mission_needs.moe: BOM and cost update effort (person-hours). Report differences from a reference BOM and estimate, missing priced items, and estimate uncertainty. This is separate from framework operating cost.

mission_needs.title: Expose early EPS design and interaction problems
mission_needs.text: Assess dynamic mission loads, energy shortages, thermal and EMC concerns, subsystem interactions, component choices, and controller constraints before hardware fabrication.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall justify designated early EPS decisions using time-dependent mission and component analyses with explicit interface conditions, applicable constraints, and unsupported checks visible.
mission_needs.moe: Coverage of decision-relevant checks and known issues found in reference fixtures. Report analysis turnaround and effort. Physical EPS defect reduction remains an empirical outcome outside framework acceptance.

mission_needs.title: Establish model and policy credibility
mission_needs.text: Use EPS and battery models with documented calibration, validity domains, electrothermal and aging assumptions, uncertainty, and evidence appropriate to the intended decision.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall distinguish predictions supported within a documented model validity domain from extrapolation and shall distinguish a predicted control-policy benefit from a demonstrated hardware benefit.
mission_needs.moe: Intended decisions covered by applicable model evidence. Report voltage, temperature, energy, health or lifetime residuals in their own units, uncertainty, runtime, and parameter-update delay. Limits require agreement for each intended use.

mission_needs.title: Support RAM requirement coverage and analysis
mission_needs.text: Identify RAM variables in requirements and generate reusable RAM analysis models from the evolving EPS and spacecraft design.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall relate designated RAM claims to requirements, design failure dependencies, generated analysis models, input assumptions, and verification evidence or explicit gaps.
mission_needs.moe: RAM model preparation effort and coverage of the declared failure and requirement set. Report model generation differences from an expert reference. No framework verdict establishes achieved spacecraft RAM.

mission_needs.title: Prepare feasible, safe and informative verification
mission_needs.text: Define EPS and component verification activities with usable procedures, conditions, equipment and DUT interfaces, safety information, observable variables, and valid synchronized telemetry.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall provide a reviewable verification proposal and evidence contract for each designated activity, with feasibility and safety decisions reserved to the responsible engineers and testing facility.
mission_needs.moe: Proposal preparation and technician clarification effort. Report missing proposal fields, evidence completeness, invalid samples, and synchronization uncertainty. Physical fault limits and timing tolerances require facility agreement.

mission_needs.title: Engineer consistent EPS flight and ground software integration
mission_needs.text: Keep command, telemetry, event, parameter, mode and recovery definitions consistent with EPS hardware and support cFS and F-Prime mappings and target resource assessment.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall produce revision-linked EPS software integration contracts, framework-specific mappings, command and mode checks, and processor, memory, timing and power evidence for the declared target configuration.
mission_needs.moe: Interface discrepancy detection and integration effort on common reference fixtures. Report dictionary and behavior coverage, configuration compatibility status, and target resource estimates or measurements. Unverified target deployment stays explicit.

mission_needs.title: Reproduce and reuse evidence for analysis and troubleshooting
mission_needs.text: Enable independent reproduction and reuse of early EPS analysis and later supplied measurements without losing configuration or validity context.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall permit an independent participant to reconstruct each designated analysis from its controlled baseline and evaluate agreement using result-specific comparison rules fixed before execution.
mission_needs.moe: Successful designated reproductions / attempted designated reproductions, independent active effort, and reconstruction gaps. Agreement limits are result-specific. Reduced use of physical replicas is a future hypothesis.

mission_needs.title: Communicate designs and justification clearly
mission_needs.text: Provide readable design views and requirement-to-design-to-evidence reviews with visible assumptions, limitations, and finding dispositions.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall provide a controlled review package from which a reviewer can locate the designated design, decision rationale, applicable evidence, and unresolved findings.
mission_needs.moe: Review preparation effort and reviewer task completion, interpretation accuracy, and clarification effort on a fixed task set. Readability needs a reviewer protocol, not an invented visual score.

mission_needs.title: Adopt and reuse the framework within team resources
mission_needs.text: Provide a declared minimum environment, learning path and reusable core suitable for contrasting EPS contexts, with adoption, adaptation and direct operating burdens visible.
mission_needs.mission_requirement: The enterprise shall complete the declared reference workflow in two contrasting EPS cases using an identified common core, declared case adaptations, and independently reconstructable environment instructions.
mission_needs.moe: Adoption and case adaptation effort (active person-hours), direct framework cost (CAD over a declared period), and case completion status. Report required computing, licenses and services. Resource ceilings require stakeholder agreement.

framework_requirements.title: Requirement record
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain each requirement as an identified record with source need, parent, rationale, observable quantities or conditions and applicable units, owner, verification method, criterion, and resolution status. A not-applicable field shall retain its rationale.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Round-trip a quantitative requirement and a qualitative demonstration requirement, including source, condition or quantity, applicable units and criterion. An inapplicable field retains rationale. An absent criterion remains unresolved and cannot acquire a verified label.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: A reviewable requirement record supports verifiability without forcing every requirement into a numerical quantity. The reported egg demonstration supports observable qualitative conditions and rationale for inapplicable fields.

framework_requirements.title: Learning and templates
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall provide requirement and traceability templates, worked EPS examples, and a guided reference workflow that covers writing criteria, linking evidence, and interpreting gaps.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Inspect the learning package and demonstrate the workflow from a declared clean start. Measure learner effort and errors without imposing an unagreed time limit.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Requirement and trace-tool learning burdens require worked guidance and a reproducible learning task, rather than an assumed user skill.

framework_requirements.title: Method applicability
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain a source-linked catalogue of requirement derivation and verification methods, standards, and activity templates with applicability, tailoring rationale, and limitations.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: For subsystem and component fixtures retrieve the chosen method and its source, conditions, tailoring decision, and excluded alternatives. A catalogue entry does not assert standards compliance.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Many methods and standards require a sourced applicability and tailoring choice. A catalogue recommendation is distinct from standards compliance.

framework_requirements.title: Bidirectional trace retrieval
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retrieve applicable links from needs and requirements to design decisions, model inputs, verification criteria and results, and retrieve the reverse paths.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Compare both query directions with the fixture relation set. Missing, ambiguous and stale endpoints remain visible.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Requirement-to-design and evidence communication burdens require both query directions and explicit gaps.

framework_requirements.title: Change impact
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall identify the requirements, EPS and non-EPS allocations, BOMs, models, software definitions, procedures, and evidence affected by a designated change.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Use seeded cross-subsystem and component changes. Compare the returned impact set and unresolved coverage with an adjudicated reference.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Reciprocal EPS/non-EPS/component changes can affect requirements, software, BOM and evidence. Impact must be evaluated across their explicit dependencies.

framework_requirements.title: Change disposition
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall issue a successor baseline for an accepted change that retains its request and failed-gate context and marks affected evidence as regenerated, stale, or unresolved.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Exercise a failed verification gate followed by correction. Preserve the prior baseline and prevent stale results from appearing current.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Failed gates and observation updates require preserved history and controlled successor evidence. A stale intermediate baseline is not a correct completed change.

framework_requirements.title: Controlled baselines
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain identified, retrievable baselines of engineering records, case configuration, and evidence with revision history and distinct identities for accepted successors.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Reconstruct two revisions after a change and compare their manifests and contents. Attempted overwrite cannot erase the retained prior baseline.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: A retrievable prior baseline and exact dependency revisions support change accountability and reconstruction.

framework_requirements.title: Semantic transfers
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall check transferred identifiers, structure, quantities, units, polarity, time bases, interface meanings, and provenance against a declared contract and retain explicit rejection findings.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Inject unit, sign, identifier and time-base mismatches. Reject incompatible transfers without replacing controlled content. Record unsupported or lossy mappings.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Manual and automated conversions can lose meaning. Unit, sign, clock and identifier checks retain a clear rejection outcome without corrupting prior content.

framework_requirements.title: Result provenance
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall associate each result with its producer, method, requirement and decision, design and hardware configuration, software and model versions, parameter set, input data, environment, and raw output.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Trace an analytical and a supplied measurement result to every applicable configuration item. An unknown identity remains a gap and blocks a contradictory validity claim.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Versions of design, hardware, software, models and data determine the applicability of each result and the context for later reconciliation.

framework_requirements.title: Independent replay
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall provide controlled instructions and dependencies to reconstruct and execute a designated analysis and compare its raw outputs using declared result-specific rules and tolerances.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: An independent participant replays a baseline from a clean declared environment. Retain logs, seeds when relevant, failures and comparison verdicts. Tolerances are fixed before replay.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Fragmentation and replica/troubleshooting concerns require independent replay under explicit result comparisons. Replay does not establish physical validity.

framework_requirements.title: Evidence and discrepancy status
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall report missing, rejected, stale, out-of-domain, failed, and unresolved evidence with its affected claim, criticality rationale, owner and disposition.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Seed each status including a critical finding. A claim affected by unresolved critical evidence cannot receive an unqualified supported or verified status.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Evidence status and critical findings must govern supported claims and review. Registration cannot conceal missing or technically inapplicable evidence.

framework_requirements.title: Candidate BOM
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall generate and revise a candidate-specific BOM from identified physical design items with assembly, quantities, part identifiers, variant and selection status, and source revision.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Compare two alternative assemblies and one component substitution with a reference BOM. Candidate alternatives remain distinct. Missing part data is reported.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Candidate multiplicity and design changes require BOM occurrence/quantity derivation tied to a distinct option and revision.

framework_requirements.title: Financial estimate
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall derive a revision-linked financial estimate from the BOM and declared additional cost categories while retaining price source, date, currency, quantity, estimate basis, uncertainty and missing data.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Recalculate a sourced-price fixture after a quantity and part change. Match reference arithmetic and preserve unknown costs. Do not import historical project costs as new framework measurements.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Cost freshness requires traceable arithmetic and source currency/date/scope, with missing prices and uncertainty preserved.

framework_requirements.title: EPS candidate comparison
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall produce a comparison of designated EPS architectures using a common requirement, assumption, evidence and criterion basis with feasibility status, raw measures, uncertainty and decision rationale.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Compare candidates with a failing requirement and incomplete evidence. Keep feasibility and unknown status separate from ranking. Any preference weights are declared before results.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: EPS choices require comparable assumptions and criteria with feasibility and unknown evidence separate from any ranking.

framework_requirements.title: Reusable EPS representation
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall provide a configurable generic EPS representation covering requirements, functions, logical and physical elements, interfaces, modes and states, with case-specific parameter and extension records.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Instantiate the representation in two contrasting cases and trace a requirement through function, allocation, interface and analysis. An extension retains its relation to the generic core.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: The introduction expressly calls for a generic EPS architecture. Functions, structure, interfaces and modes must remain reusable across declared cases.

framework_requirements.title: Dynamic mission composition
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall compose time-dependent subsystem demand, duty cycles, schedules and mode transitions with orbit, attitude, irradiance, eclipse, thermal conditions and EPS supply and protection behavior.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Use a fixture whose average budget passes while a coupled load and illumination event creates a transient shortage. Inspect inputs, interactions and event timing against a reference calculation.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Dynamic demand, supply/protection and attitude/illumination interactions require time histories as well as averages.

framework_requirements.title: Requirement parameter derivation
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall record how sourced component power and thermal characteristics and subsystem behavior become EPS or component requirement parameters, including units, uncertainties, allowable ranges and criterion decisions.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Derive a fixture allocation from datasheet and supplied measurement inputs using a declared method. Preserve assumptions and flag unsupported ranges and undecided pass/fail values.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Pass/fail and update burdens require a sourced derivation from component properties and subsystem behavior to requirement criteria.

framework_requirements.title: Discipline model integration
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall exchange identified EPS component and design data with declared electrical, thermal, EMC and CAD analysis tools and retain model mappings, applicable outputs and unsupported checks.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Every electrical, thermal, EMC and CAD exchange profile required by the frozen minimum shall complete its reference request/result exchange and declared identity, quantity, unit, meaning and revision checks. Retain unsupported mappings and development gaps. A missing required profile remains not verified or undetermined and cannot pass V18. A narrower minimum requires a reviewed scope disposition before evaluation.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Specialist electrical, thermal, EMC and CAD analyses require declared placement, checked mappings and visible unsupported behavior.

framework_requirements.title: Early verification scenarios
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall execute or coordinate declared virtual EPS and component verification scenarios for dynamic loads, supply changes, protection events, rare faults, and controller electrical and timing constraints.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Retain stimulus, conditions, expected response, outputs and status for nominal and failure fixtures. Unsupported behavior and physical validation needs are explicit, including COTS evidence gaps.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Prototype dependence and hazardous conditions motivate bounded virtual scenarios with explicit expected responses and residual physical obligations.

framework_requirements.title: Battery model coupling
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall integrate identified battery electrical, thermal and degradation models with mission loads and retain the states, health and lifetime outputs, assumptions and uncertainty supported by each model.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Replay fresh and aged battery fixtures under different load and temperature profiles. Verify coupling and provenance. Missing aging mechanisms and latent-state uncertainty remain visible.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Energy and lifetime uncertainty depends on coupled load, temperature, health and represented degradation mechanisms. Model-dependent outputs need visible limits.

framework_requirements.title: Intended-use credibility
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall associate each analytical verification claim with the model intended use, tested validity domain, calibration and validation evidence, uncertainty and acceptable prediction-error rule.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Exercise an in-domain and an extrapolated claim. Separate calibration from validation data where available. Flag untested domains and absent error limits. Prediction accuracy limits require prior agreement.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Credible verification requires intended-use adequacy, separate calibration/validation context, error rules and an explicit extrapolation verdict.

framework_requirements.title: Model update workflow
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall use supplied measurements to create an identified calibration or parameter-update record with data quality, prior and revised parameters, residuals and affected analyses.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Apply a measurement fixture, compare the declared calibration result with a reference, retain both parameter revisions, and flag analyses affected by drift or update.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Delayed measurement feedback and parameter drift require a traceable calibration proposal and reanalysis impact, rather than silent overwrites.

framework_requirements.title: Fidelity and execution contract
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall record the selected model fidelity, execution environment, time step, measured or estimated runtime and interface delays for each declared SIL or HIL interaction profile.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Profile a declared executable model and replay timestamped input/output fixtures. Real-time suitability remains unresolved until the applicable hardware and deadline are verified.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Fidelity and runtime conflicts require a declared timing profile. Fast numerical steps alone do not establish hardware-loop compatibility.

framework_requirements.title: Controller policy assessment
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall compare designated charging and power-management policies under declared load, thermal, health, electrical and timing conditions with safety constraints and policy-specific outcome evidence.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Replay a baseline and a changed policy against the same fixture conditions. A model prediction cannot be labeled a demonstrated hardware improvement. Retain pending SIL, HIL or hardware evidence.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Accurate battery predictions and safe/effective controller policies are different claims. Policy comparison needs common conditions and separate outcome evidence.

framework_requirements.title: Anomaly assessment
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall compare time-correlated EPS telemetry with modeled expected behavior while retaining operating mode, model validity, degradation and sensor uncertainty, and alternative fault explanations.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Use nominal, degrading, noisy and injected-fault fixtures. Retain residuals and diagnoses with TP, FP and FN against an expert reference. No pre-threshold detection capability is presumed.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Subtle anomalies, normal degradation and sensor error require mode-aware expected/observed comparison and retained alternative explanations.

framework_requirements.title: RAM requirement coverage
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall identify the RAM variables and failure assumptions applicable to designated EPS and spacecraft requirements and report their verification-method coverage and gaps.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Compare the declared RAM variable and requirement set with a reference. Report analysis, inspection, demonstration or test rationale without forcing every claim to use analysis.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: RAM coverage gaps require named variables, failure assumptions and justified verification methods without substituting analysis for mandatory testing.

framework_requirements.title: RAM model generation
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall generate a declared RAM analysis representation from identified functions, components and failure dependencies with traceable transformation rules and sourced or missing reliability data.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Generate an FMEA, fault tree or other justified representation for a reference design and its changed variant. Compare entities and dependencies with an expert model. Missing probabilities cannot become factual reliability estimates.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: The cost of RAM modeling motivates traceable generation from design/failure dependencies. Missing reliability inputs remain unknown.

framework_requirements.title: Verification activity record
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain each EPS or component verification activity with requirement, method, DUT baseline, applicable quantities or observable conditions, inputs, expected response, criterion, evidence variables and status. An inapplicable field shall retain its rationale.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Inspect quantitative analysis/test and qualitative inspection/demonstration fixtures against their method-specific fields. Check the applicable quantity or observable condition, criterion, expected response and evidence. An inapplicable field retains rationale. Missing mandatory fields, failed gates and unresolved criteria remain explicit and prevent an unsupported verdict.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Subsystem/component verification burdens require a method-specific activity contract with criterion and observable response. Qualitative demonstrations use observable conditions.

framework_requirements.title: Facility proposal
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall produce a technician-readable verification proposal that specifies conditions, equipment and fixture identities, DUT connections, stimulus sequence, observations and evidence-generation procedure.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: A technician or qualified proxy checks a fixture proposal against a declared completeness checklist and identifies how equipment interacts with the DUT. Facility feasibility remains a separate decision.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Technicians need an understandable procedure and equipment/DUT interaction specification to assess feasibility.

framework_requirements.title: Safety declaration
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall include hazards, battery and electronics operating limits, fault-injection envelope, isolation, abort conditions and responsible safety-review status in each proposed physical verification activity.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Use a safe virtual fault fixture and an incomplete physical proposal. Missing limits or approval status block a ready-for-physical-execution label. The framework does not authorize laboratory operations.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Battery/electronics damage risk requires declared limits, aborts and external safety disposition. Virtual checks do not authorize hardware work.

framework_requirements.title: Evidence timing
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall record the time base, sampling and synchronization rules and known measurement, calculation and output delays for applied stimuli, responses and telemetry.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Align a known timestamp fixture and expose injected skew and missing timing metadata. Report alignment error or uncertainty against the agreed profile, with no invented global limit.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Stimulus, measurement and simulation delays affect correspondence. A clock and delay contract supports accountable alignment.

framework_requirements.title: Telemetry quality
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall check expected telemetry channels, units, timestamps, completeness and sensor validity conditions and preserve raw samples, invalid values and processing masks.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Inject missing samples, inactive sensors and invalid values. Do not treat inactive invalid readings as valid measurements. Match the fixture quality verdict and retained raw data.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Inactive and invalid telemetry can falsely imply behavior. Keep raw samples and masks and explicitly assess channel completeness.

framework_requirements.title: Shared software definitions
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain revision-linked EPS command, telemetry, event and parameter definitions with identifiers, types, units, ranges and encodings mapped to hardware, functional software and ground dictionaries.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Compare model, flight and ground fixtures against a shared contract. Detect a changed definition in one representation and report every affected mapping.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Duplicated definitions and different hardware/software groupings require a shared semantic service contract across model, flight and ground artifacts.

framework_requirements.title: Flight framework mapping
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall produce or coordinate checked mappings of the EPS software contract to declared cFS software-bus and F-Prime typed-connection profiles and identify behavior and implementation gaps.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Round-trip or validate reference message and port mappings in both profiles. Declare framework version and unsupported exports. Architecture or dictionary generation is distinct from mission-specific functionality.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: cFS publish-subscribe and F-Prime typed topology require separate versioned mappings. Supported architecture export is distinct from mission behavior generation.

framework_requirements.title: Command and recovery contract
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall specify and check EPS command preconditions, order, expected effects, rejection and failure behavior, mode transitions and recovery responsibilities across EPS, telemetry, fault-management and safe-mode functions.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Replay nominal, rejected and recovery sequences with a qualified software reference. Confirm functional flow and ownership without claiming deployment of flight software.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Command execution, mode transitions and distributed recovery responsibilities require checked guards/effects and ownership contracts.

framework_requirements.title: Target integration assessment
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall retain a versioned OBC, operating-system, flight-framework and toolchain configuration with compatibility evidence and processor, memory, timing and power budget evidence for EPS functions.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Inspect a build/deployment profile and reference resource records. Distinguish measurements, estimates and unknown target compatibility. Check against mission-supplied allocations when available.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: OBC/OS/framework/toolchain choices affect feasibility and processor, memory, timing and power budgets. Evidence must name a target and distinguish estimates from measurements.

framework_requirements.title: Readable design views
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall produce filtered context, structure, interface and selected-design views from controlled EPS records with identifiers, units, legends and links to the represented baseline.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Compare generated views with a fixture model and apply a declared reviewer task checklist. Assess correctness and readability without proliferating requirement, measure, scenario or state diagrams.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Design review concerns require accurate filtered representations of accepted content at readable scale. View generation alone proves no review benefit.

framework_requirements.title: Review package
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall assemble the designated requirement, decision, design, evidence, assumptions, uncertainty, validity limits, findings and dispositions into a baseline-linked review package.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: An independent reviewer locates the designated claims and evidence and records findings and outcomes. Keep author status, reviewer outcome and approval authority distinct.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Requirement/design/evidence communication requires a baseline-linked justification package with finding disposition and separate reviewer authority.

framework_requirements.title: Minimum adoption and measurement package
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall declare prerequisites, resource footprint, licenses, dependencies and learning instructions for its minimum workflow and record adoption, adaptation, change, reproduction and direct-cost observations under one evaluation protocol.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Demonstrate the minimum workflow from a clean declared environment. Record wall-clock time separately from active person-hours and state the cost period and inclusions. Unknown cost stays unknown.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: Resource fit and adoption burdens require minimum prerequisites and common task/time/cost protocols. No implementation-specific benefit follows from architecture alone.

framework_requirements.title: Contrasting-case reuse
framework_requirements.text: The framework shall apply an identified common core to two predefined contrasting EPS cases using declared parameters, mappings and extensions and retain case outcomes and any core changes.
framework_requirements.proposed_acceptance: Complete the same declared workflow in both cases without undeclared or post hoc core changes. If the core changes, rebaseline and rerun both cases before a reuse claim. No implementation or successful outcome is asserted here.
framework_requirements.derivation_rationale: The introduction requires two contrasting cases with no post hoc core changes. Fix the profiles before evaluation and retain failed trials and any later rebaseline.

additional_source_context.text: The current project is intended as a precedent for that large-scale ambition, covering the electrical power subsystem in its lifecycle phases prior to commissiong or developing hardware (early phases), and is founded in the experience gained in previous EPS design efforts at ASCEND. Therefore, the particular problem addressed by this project is:
additional_source_context.meaning: Early lifecycle before commissioning or developing EPS hardware.

additional_source_context.text: The lifecycle of the framework, which crucially must be distinguished from the lifecycle of its EPS system of interest, follows the Object-Oriented Systems Engineering Methodology (OOSEM) \cite{friedenthal2014practical}. The engineering process is formalized by using the Systems Modeling Language version 2 (SysML v2) to represent requirements and their solution. Candidate solutions remain free to implement other methods, languages, formats, and tools as part of their behavior.
additional_source_context.meaning: OOSEM process formalized in SysML v2. Candidate implementations retain freedom of methods, languages, formats and tools.

additional_source_context.text:
A project proposal was written before a complete understanding of the stakeholders' needs was achieved. Said proposal defined objectives, deliverables, indicators, and deadlines that form the research contribution baseline, without specifying the framework itself.
The assessment of the objective deliverables against their indicators and deadlines will be carried out separately from the framework integration and verification that happens within OOSEM (Section \ref{section:integrate-and-verify-system}).
additional_source_context.meaning: Research deliverable assessment is distinct from framework integration and verification.

steps.action: Declare scope, decision, resources, core and permitted tailoring. Obtain sourced guidance and retain the case configuration.
Capture requirements and criteria including qualitative demonstrations and RAM obligations. Bind EPS options to sourced component, BOM, price and resource information.
Run common scenario comparisons, assess applicability and preserve admissible evidence and remaining verification needs.
Review options, trace chains and unknowns. Record the engineer disposition, freeze the package and independently replay a designated analysis. Capture reviewed learning.

alternatives: Missing property, criterion, quote or applicable model evidence leaves comparison or decision status unresolved.
Incompatible transfers retain findings and prior baselines. A failed independent replay remains a failed task.
The two contrasting profiles are fixed before evaluation. A common-core defect is retained as a failed trial and requires a separate rebaseline and both-case rerun.

mission_scenarios.name: Process a coupled load and EPS service change

steps.action: Propose a payload or attitude change against a baseline. Scope upstream and downstream impacts including demand, limits, battery models, service definitions, BOM/RAM/resource evidence and verification.
Revise supply and shared hardware/flight/ground contracts. Apply supported target mappings and check command, mode, recovery and resource obligations.

Execute changed time-dependent generation/load/policy scenarios, inspect applicability and evaluate relevant early EPS and service criteria. An average energy surplus cannot close a dynamic obligation.
Disposition proposed revisions and residual actions. Retain the successor with stale/updated status, replay required evidence and expose both directions of impact.

alternatives: Unknown cFS/F-Prime/OS compatibility or target resources blocks the corresponding supported claim.
Unit, telemetry or guard/effect mismatches and unsupported validity domains retain explicit findings.
A successor baseline is a controlled intermediate outcome. Favorable change time or effort is reported only after the declared correctness rule passes.

mission_scenarios.name: Resolve a failed protection gate and prepare safe later testing

steps.action: Preserve the failed or inconclusive assessment with raw stimuli, observations, states, setup and revisions. Check channel validity, synchronization, intended-use evidence and alternative explanations.
Propose and disposition a calibration, property or design update. Repeat affected scenarios while keeping safety, prediction agreement and policy effectiveness as separate claims.
Compile equipment/DUT interaction, procedure, capture, limits and abort/recovery requirements. Retain the technician feasibility and safety disposition for later physical testing.
If approved-setup observations are later supplied, assess quality and create proposed credibility/parameter revisions. Scope prior-decision impact, reanalyse and review residual actions.

alternatives: Missing validation, fault limits, protection or timing capability yields blocked or inconclusive handoff.
Inactive channels, missing active-unit mappings, clock skew or model extrapolation remain flagged and cannot become valid measurements.
Simulation agreement cannot authorize hazardous hardware work. Framework verification uses replay and review fixtures, without hazardous physical tests.

mission_requirements.text: The EPS engineering enterprise shall produce reviewable framework-supported EPS and component requirements whose source, observable quantities or conditions, verification method, criterion, and unresolved decisions are explicit.
The enterprise shall identify the affected evidence for each designated change and issue a successor baseline with regenerated or explicitly stale evidence and retained discrepancy status.
The enterprise shall obtain a revision-linked BOM and financial estimate for each designated EPS candidate, with sourced prices, quantities, assumptions, uncertainty, and missing cost data visible.

The enterprise shall justify designated early EPS decisions using time-dependent mission and component analyses with explicit interface conditions, applicable constraints, and unsupported checks visible.

The enterprise shall distinguish predictions supported within a documented model validity domain from extrapolation and shall distinguish a predicted control-policy benefit from a demonstrated hardware benefit.
The enterprise shall relate designated RAM claims to requirements, design failure dependencies, generated analysis models, input assumptions, and verification evidence or explicit gaps.

The enterprise shall provide a reviewable verification proposal and evidence contract for each designated activity, with feasibility and safety decisions reserved to the responsible engineers and testing facility.

The enterprise shall produce revision-linked EPS software integration contracts, framework-specific mappings, command and mode checks, and processor, memory, timing and power evidence for the declared target configuration.

The enterprise shall permit an independent participant to reconstruct each designated analysis from its controlled baseline and evaluate agreement using result-specific comparison rules fixed before execution.
The enterprise shall provide a controlled review package from which a reviewer can locate the designated design, decision rationale, applicable evidence, and unresolved findings.

The enterprise shall complete the declared reference workflow in two contrasting EPS cases using an identified common core, declared case adaptations, and independently reconstructable environment instructions.

reported_as_is_narrative.exact_text:
ASCEND is currently associated to a Rocketry Team and an Avionics Team of a student club.
The Rocketry Team operates on requirements given by Rocketry Competition Organizers.
The requirements are stated in terms of the target maximum height or maximum acceleration of the rocket.
One competition imposed the requirement of launching and returning to ground an egg without breaking it, which can only be validated via demonstration.
The Team Captains convert the requirements of a competition to atomic tasks.
Tasks are performed by any club member and approved by senior members.
The club performs the PDR, CDR, and FRR review gates.

There is a large emphasis on technology reuse at the club, so most tasks are formulated as atomic edits to existing designs.
Furthermore, most of the tasks for a particular competition involve development activities like PCB manufacturing, soldering, and assembly.
One observed task involved adding a COTS to a PCB, which was specified in the task title. The task was broken down into subtasks, one of which required to connect a capacitor to the COTS, possibly prescribed by its datasheet.

The competition requirements include the radio communications technologies allowed for rocket launch commands and telemetry.
Thus, radio transceivers are some of the first COTS chosen for rocket designs.
The egg mission also introduced a payload consisting of 1U unit with a mechanically damping material to protect the egg, and heat pumps to maintain its temperature within a range inspired by an incubator machine.

Multiple lithium-ion cells were used to power the latest revision of the egg incubator payload.
To size them, a power budget was generated by consulting the datasheets of the already chosen components and extracting "on" and "off" power consumption values, then estimating the duty cycle of each component for one launch.
The duty cycle of telemetry components is estimated from the telemetry frequency requirements of the competition. For the rest of the components, it is conservatively assumed that they are always on.

A PCB design was observed consisting of multiple boards connected perpendicularly via PCI to a backplane that was the size of a 1U face.
Status indicator LEDs were observed for 3.3 and 5 volt buses.
The power source of the payload is verified experimentally.
The payload is fully assembled and set to provide telemetry at a realistic frequency while powered by the battery.
